stories.headline: Iran to open 'communication channel' with US after indirect talks in Qatar on ceasefire

key_facts.fact: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi announced on July 1 that Tehran will establish a 'communication channel' with Washington to report breaches of the memorandum of understanding signed two weeks ago to end the US-Israel war on Iran.
key_facts.excerpt: Tehran says it will establish a 'communication channel' with Washington to report breaches of the memorandum of understanding (MoU), signed between them two weeks ago, to end the US-Israel war on Iran.

key_facts.fact: Indirect technical talks between Iran and the US were held in Qatar on Wednesday July 1 to discuss the flow of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and securing the ceasefire amid breaches since the MoU was signed.
key_facts.excerpt: The US-Iran indirect talks in the Qatari capital were held to discuss the flow of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and securing the ceasefire amid breaches since the MoU was signed last month.

key_facts.fact: The MoU, brokered by Qatar and Pakistan, includes a 60-day ceasefire, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and a timeframe for a final deal to permanently end the war and reach an agreement on Iran's nuclear programme.
key_facts.excerpt: The memorandum, brokered by Qatar and Pakistan, includes a 60-day ceasefire, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and a timeframe for a final deal to permanently end the war.

key_facts.fact: US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday he could not guarantee that Washington would not return to combat before next month's MoU deadline.
key_facts.excerpt: US Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday said he could not guarantee that Washington would not return to combat before next month's MoU deadline.

key_facts.fact: In Doha, Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani met US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and reaffirmed Qatar's continued mediation efforts alongside Pakistan.
key_facts.excerpt: In Doha on Wednesday, Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani met US special envoy Steve Witkoff and Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner.

stories.headline: Ukraine strikes Russian missile-sensor institute in Penza and Ufa oil refinery deep inside Russia

key_facts.fact: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed on July 1, 2026 that Ukraine struck NIIFI in Penza, Russia, a Roscosmos enterprise producing sensor components for Iskander, Bulava, Topol-M and Kh-101 missiles.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelenskyy confirmed on July 1, 2026, that Ukraine struck NIIFI in Penza, a Roscosmos enterprise producing sensor components for Iskander, Bulava, Topol-M, and Kh-101 missiles.

key_facts.fact: A simultaneous strike hit an oil refinery in Ufa, Russia, approximately 1,300 km from the front line, marking the second Ukrainian attack on that facility.
key_facts.excerpt: A simultaneous strike hit an oil refinery in Ufa, approximately 1,300 km from the front line, marking the second Ukrainian attack on that facility.

key_facts.fact: The NIIFI institute operates under the Roscosmos state corporation and supplies precision sensor systems for Su-34 and Su-57 fighter aircraft and Kh-101 and Kh-59 cruise missiles, output that Russia cannot easily import given Western sanctions.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility struck is the Scientific Research Institute of Physical Measurements, known by its Russian acronym NIIFI, a state enterprise operating under the Roscosmos state corporation that supplies precision sensor systems across virtually every major class of Russian offensive weapon.

key_facts.fact: Russia followed with a massive missile and drone attack on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities; the latest reports put the toll at at least 17 killed and more than 80 injured.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian missile and drone strikes targeted Kyiv and several Ukrainian cities, killing at least 17 people and injuring over 80.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine's Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said on July 1 that intensified drone strikes on occupied Crimea were made possible by a 'new technological stage of the war,' with Russia finding it increasingly difficult to resolve one crisis after another.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine's increasingly frequent drone strikes on occupied Crimea have been made possible by a 'new technological stage of the war,' Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov said on July 1.

stories.headline: FDA approves Orca Bio's Tregzi, the first regulatory T-cell therapy for blood cancer transplant patients

key_facts.fact: The FDA announced on June 30, 2026 that it approved Tregzi (Orca-T), a donor-derived cellular immunotherapy from Orca Bio, to improve chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD)-free survival in adults undergoing allogeneic stem cell transplantation.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA announced on June 30, 2026 that it has approved Tregzi for the treatment of chronic graft-versus-host disease (GVHD)... Tregzi, a donor-derived cellular immunotherapy developed by Orca Biosystems, is the first regulatory T-cell-based immunotherapy approved.

key_facts.fact: In the Phase 3 PRECISION-T trial of 187 patients, 78% of Tregzi recipients achieved 1-year chronic GVHD-free survival versus 38.4% with standard transplant.
key_facts.excerpt: PRECISION-T (n=187) met its primary endpoint: 1-year chronic GVHD-free survival was 78% with Tregzi versus 38.4% with standard transplant.

key_facts.fact: Serious chronic GVHD at 1 year occurred in 12.6% of Tregzi recipients versus 44% with standard transplant, and overall survival was 94% with Tregzi versus 83% with conventional transplant.
key_facts.excerpt: GVHD-free and relapse-free survival was more than double for patients given Tregzi, while overall survival was 94% with Tregzi and 83% with alloHSCT.

key_facts.fact: Tregzi is Orca Bio's first approved therapy; the trial enrolled patients with acute myeloid leukemia, acute lymphoblastic leukemia, myelodysplastic syndrome and mixed-phenotype acute leukemia, and the application had Orphan Drug and Regenerative Medicine Advanced Therapy designations.
key_facts.excerpt: Tregzi is also Orca's first approved therapy, 'validating the company's high-precision platform and the potential of its pipeline,' the California-based company said.

stories.headline: Fed Chair Warsh signals focus on inflation, likely foreclosing rate cuts Trump has sought

key_facts.fact: New Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said on Wednesday July 1 that the central bank would remain independent and seek to bring down inflation, likely foreclosing the rate cuts President Trump has sought.
key_facts.excerpt: New Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh said Wednesday that the central bank would remain independent and seek to bring down inflation, likely foreclosing the rate cuts President Donald Trump has sought.

key_facts.fact: Warsh, who replaced Jerome Powell as chair on May 22, has shifted from calling for lower rates last year to signaling a focus on getting inflation down; Wall Street investors expect the Fed could hike its key rate as soon as September from about 3.6% to roughly 3.9%.
key_facts.excerpt: Wall Street investors expect the Fed could hike its key interest rate as soon as in September, from its current level of about 3.6% to roughly 3.9%.

key_facts.fact: Inflation rose to a three-year high of 4.2% in May, pushed up partly by the war's impact on gas prices, though Warsh said there are signs the threat of persistent inflation has moderated.
key_facts.excerpt: inflation rising to a three-year high of 4.2% in May, pushed... war's impact on gas prices.

key_facts.fact: The June ADP report released July 1 showed US private employers added 98,000 jobs, missing the Reuters forecast of 118,000, while planned layoffs dropped 53% to 45,849 in June.
key_facts.excerpt: Private employment rose by 98,000 jobs last month after an unrevised gain of 122,000 in May... Economists polled by Reuters had forecast private employment would increase by 118,000.

stories.headline: Oil posts worst quarter since 2020 as Persian Gulf supply recovers and US-Iran talks ease fears

key_facts.fact: ICE Brent closed out its weakest quarter since 2020, down a little more than 38% in the April-June period, dragged down by growing confidence that Persian Gulf crude flows are on the mend.
key_facts.excerpt: The oil market finished the second quarter yesterday weak, with ICE Brent down a little more than 38% in the April-June period, the weakest quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2020.

key_facts.fact: US WTI crude futures settled at $68.58 on July 1, the lowest settle going back to the start of the Iran War, after oil fell roughly 2% amid optimism over US-Iran talks.
key_facts.excerpt: Crude oil futures settle at $68.58. Lowest settle going back to the start of the Iran War.

key_facts.fact: Brent fell by around $45 a barrel in the second quarter, its largest quarterly loss since the global financial crisis in 2008, while US crude futures fell around $31, their largest quarterly loss since 2020.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent fell by around $45 a barrel in the second quarter of this year, its largest quarterly loss since the global financial crisis in 2008. U.S. crude futures, meanwhile, fell by around $31, their largest quarterly loss since 2020.

key_facts.fact: US crude oil production climbed to a record 13.93m barrels per day in April, up 1.6% month-on-month, helping offset supply losses from the Persian Gulf.
key_facts.excerpt: Supply climbed to a record 13.93m b/d, up 1.6% month-on-month and 3.5% higher year-on-year.

stories.headline: Alibaba and Ant unit AUS to pay $600M to settle US probe over illegal drug sales on its platforms

key_facts.fact: Alibaba Group and its US-based payment processor AUS Merchant Services agreed to pay a combined $600 million and enter non-prosecution agreements with the DOJ, announced Wednesday July 1, over failing to prevent illegal product sales into the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. and its U.S.-based payment processor, AUS Merchant Services, will pay a combined $600 million to resolve allegations they failed to stop merchants from selling and importing illegal pharmaceuticals, controlled substances, regulated chemicals and pill-making equipment.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba admitted that between January 2016 and December 2024, roughly 80,000 unlawful product sales involving US imports violated the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and other federal laws, with a combined value over $200 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba admitted that between January 2016 and December 2024, roughly 80,000 unlawful product sales involving imports into the U.S. violated the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act, and other federal laws.

key_facts.fact: Under the agreement Alibaba will pay a $125 million criminal penalty and forfeit $200 million, while AUS Merchant Services will pay an $85 million criminal penalty and forfeit $190 million.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba will pay a $125 million criminal penalty and forfeit $200 million, while AUS Merchant Services will pay an $85 million criminal penalty and forfeit $190 million.

key_facts.fact: AUS Merchant Services, a unit of Ant Group that operates Alipay, admitted its anti-money laundering compliance program failed to prevent some merchants from using its services to facilitate the illegal sales; law enforcement conducted more than 40 undercover purchases during the probe.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S.-based payment processor's anti-money laundering compliance program failed to prevent some merchants from using its services to facilitate the sale and importation of prohibited products.

stories.headline: ULA launches Amazon Leo 8 on Atlas V, the rocket's final flight outside Starliner missions

key_facts.fact: A United Launch Alliance Atlas V 551 rocket launched 29 Amazon Leo (formerly Project Kuiper) broadband satellites from Cape Canaveral early Thursday, July 2, 2026, at 12:30:15 a.m. EDT.
key_facts.excerpt: ULA's Atlas V rocket delivered another batch of satellites for Amazon Leo... Launch Date and Time: July 2, 2026 at 12:30:15 a.m. EDT (0430:15 UTC).

key_facts.fact: The Amazon Leo LA-08 mission was the last time the Atlas V flies a mission for anything other than Starliner, as ULA winds down the rocket line in favor of its new Vulcan rocket.
key_facts.excerpt: Thursday morning's launch of Atlas V and Amazon Leo LA-08 will be the last time the venerable rocket flies a mission for anything other than Starliner.

key_facts.fact: Atlas V debuted on August 21, 2002 and over its 109-launch history has flown the Curiosity and Perseverance Mars rovers, the New Horizons probe to Pluto, the Juno mission to Jupiter, and 58 national security missions.
key_facts.excerpt: Over its 109 launch history, Atlas V has launched the Curiosity and Perseverance rovers toward Mars, the New Horizons probe to Pluto, the Juno mission to Jupiter, the Starliner missions and 58 national security missions.

key_facts.fact: Amazon's Leo constellation is planned to include more than 3,000 satellites (3,236 planned) in low Earth orbit to deliver broadband internet to customers beyond the reach of existing networks.
key_facts.excerpt: The initial Amazon constellation will include more than 3,000 satellites working together in coordinated orbits around Earth.
